entries.en: We want to assess any potential risk to asari copyrights.
Everyone here knows who you are, dull stone.
That makes you ideal for my job. You are a known quantity. Or so Vargas will think.
He will assume you are here to investigate his company's dirty laundry. That will distract him from your--my--real intentions.
You will present yourself as a buyer. On behalf of the Spectres or the Alliance. Discuss their military enhancement programs.
Your real objective will be to distract him. I will give you a device that will crack into his personal wireless network.
It will upload a variety of monitoring viruses. They will infiltrate Binary Helix when he logs onto their intranet.
Spectres are known for their moral flexibility. You more than most.
Do you think that Binary Helix obeys all the laws? That they do not spy on other companies?
Very well, Spectre. I will be on my way.
Money, of course. I would be well-paid for this. So would you. Five hundred credits.
Excellent. Here is the cracking device. You will know it is done when it beeps.
I hope to hear from you soon.
Let me know what you decide.
My mistake, obviously.
I don't know anything about Binary Helix. What would I talk to Vargas about?
He's right there. Why not talk to him yourself?
Do you know who I am?
Strange people skulking in corners have gotten me in trouble before.
You think this uniform's just for show? My job is to enforce the law, not break it.
If I see them behaving badly, I'll shut them down. However I see fit. In the meantime, there's you. Trying to bribe a Spectre.
News reports and rumor take all the fun out of life. All right, I'm interested.
What they might be doing somewhere else doesn't justify my acting against them here.
No, I don't suppose they're clean, either.
Interesting plan. I'm in.
Tell me what you know about Vargas.
I'll go see him now.
I'll think about it.
Whatever you need done, ask someone else. I'm busy.
Why me? What's this about?
Why can't you do this?
Why should I trust you?
This is illegal.
What's my reward?
Brief me.
Then I will find someone else. But I doubt you will find another job that pays 500 credits to listen to a salesman.
He is impatient with those who waste his time. I tried to get him distracted and off-topic. He concluded I was not interested in his company's services.
I noticed he has a "tell." When a topic makes him nervous or uncomfortable, he has a tendency to rub the back of his neck.
If you see that, press him on the subject. It may distract him enough to keep him talking.
Thank you. You will not see me again, Spectre.
I would appreciate any help you can offer.
I need help duping Rafael Vargas, a Binary Helix sales rep.
I told Vargas what you put me up to.
He figured out what I was up to, and left.
Your toy did its job.
I'm still working on Vargas.
Everything went as planned. You should see results soon.
I'm not going to help you. I've got other things to do.
Sorry. I shouldn't get involved in this. Here's your cracking device.
Now you're talking my language. I'll finish it.
All right. I guess I'm not that busy.
I told him about you.
Vargas caught me.
No progress yet.
[LIE] It's done.
I quit.
This is wrong.
That's good money.
I'll finish it.
The job
I see. May I ask why?
You have a unique perspective. Devious, one might say.
None taken. I would have done the same.
I believe I should get offworld now. Quickly.
I shall do so directly, Spectre. Excuse me.
Marvelous. Weeks of work lost for no reason.
Unfortunate. But I cannot blame you for sharing my lack of success.
I will need to find another avenue to access Binary Helix.
Not to worry. I will get what I want in the end.
For what? Scaring off the mark? I do not blame you, but do not presume too much.
Luck is no substitute for planning.
Excellent. I will transfer 500 credits to your account.
Did I say 500 credits? I meant 750.
As will I.
Good day, Spectre.
So you said.
Very well. Let me know when it is done.
You were breaking the law. By spying, and by bribing me. He'll be on guard against you now. That's worse than a slap-on-the-wrist fine, isn't it?
He figured out I was playing him. I'm not taking the heat for you. No offense.
One corrupt corporation is as good as another to me. Next time, take your little games elsewhere.
I don't need a reason. I'm a Spectre.
I wish I could have been more help.
Wait. What about my money?
I don't get any kind of reward for this?
Good luck with that.
Only 500? All right. I thought you might have wanted to provide more. Since you couldn't do it yourself, I mean.
I could easily call Mr. Vargas and tell him what I just did.
You're a criminal.
He caught me.
You're both irritating.
Reward.
More.
I have assembled a dossier on Vargas. If you would like, I could brief you on his behavior patterns.
A pleasure doing business with you. I'll be on my way.
That'll do nicely. I'll be going now.
Brief me on Vargas.
Now, where were we?
Shepard. You never did answer my question.
That's correct. Rafael Vargas, Sales. Were you interested in our services?
It was my understanding that the Alliance contracted to MarsGene for its enhancement programs.
It was my understanding that the Citadel contracted to a salarian corporation for its enhancement programs.
A sound business practice. Excuse my hesitation. I've never heard a government accused of good business sense.
You have my full attention, Shepard. I'm merely getting a handle on my negotiating position.
Just getting the facts in order. If you want to give us a second chance, I'll be here.
Mr. Vargas? Commander Shepard, Systems Alliance Military. I understand you work for Binary Helix?
Mr. Vargas? I'm Commander Shepard, a Spectre. I understand you work for Binary Helix?
It's customary to perform minor genetic upgrades upon enlistment. I've been assigned to see what BH has to offer.
I'm sure you know that we pass a new budget every fiscal year. If it delivers a better soldier, contracts can change.
Mr. Vargas, I'm here to talk business with you. If you'd rather speculate on politics, I can visit another gen-eng firm.
I can see you're not interested in discussing business right now. I'll come back later.
Just passing by.
I'm an Alliance marine.
That's correct.
That's irrelevant.
I might be. That depends on what sort of offer your company can make.
If the price is right.
I've notified my company of the asari plans.
Shepard, this is a field in which improvements of 2% are dramatic enough to patent.
I find it difficult to believe you would be sent to investigate this with such poor background knowledge.
I can get you those improvements for 30K credits per head.
For a bulk order, I can work in a sensory enhancement package. Guaranteed 20/15 vision and hearing from 12 to 22,000 hertz.
I suppose. My own job is to "count beans."
It does take time to upgrade a body with adjusted DNA. Skin cells could be replaced in two weeks, but the liver takes over a year, and the skeleton, a decade.
For front-line units, we can speed the process with full-system transfusions and injections to stimulate regrowth. It would still take six months to see results.
I'll give you a cautious "probably." There is a standard discount for bulk orders, but I can't authorize that.
I can push it upstairs. I'm sure someone will get back to you on it.
Absolutely. That's the standard rate. Of course, if the government moves forward with this on an official level, there might be some additional discounts.
I have to admit, it surprised me that you were here for business.
There are many development projects on Noveria. Some not entirely legal.
Certainly not! Our corporate reputation is sterling.
I can assure you, all of Binary Helix's operations on Noveria are strictly on-the-level.
Yeah, I'll keep that in mind.
Sure they are.
Yeah, I've heard that before.
I'll keep that in mind.
We'll keep that in mind.
I'll keep that in mind. Of course, we don't perform espionage on our competitors. That would be illegal.
My apologies. I shouldn't have belabored the point.
I'm beginning to. It's obvious you have no knowledge of genetics.
Which makes it highly unlikely you were sent by the Alliance.
Which makes it highly unlikely you were sent by the Citadel.
A cracking device. Full of viruses, I expect. Our IT people can isolate them, use them to feed the asari false data.
I'm disappointed in you, Commander. I thought your kind were above this sort of thing.
If you'll excuse me.
All I know is that you're wasting my time.
Then you should go to a gene clinic somewhere. I handle corporate accounts worth millions of credits.
Good day, Commander.
I suppose. My apologies. Your manner is rather informal for a business meeting.
Of course, Commander Shepard.
We look forward to hearing from the Alliance.
